text: Morholt, also spelled Morhold, was an Irish hero. He was a giant warrior who came each year to the land of king Mark of Cornwall. He claimed a tribute or tax there from the Cornish folk. The strong knight Tristan killed him, almost dying from Morholt's poisoned sword. The wound festered until Tristan found healing. Tristan later fell in love with Morholt's niece, the fair Iseult. Iseult was promised to king Mark, yet she and Tristan shared a fateful passion. Morholt's death set in motion the famous tragedy of the two lovers.

okr.objective: Document the Irish hero Morholt and his death at Tristan's hands.
